base_row.source: n8n fabric process hermes-learning (2026-10-15, AGENTS.md §23.23; packets docs/ops/packets/n8n-hermes-learning-flow-20261015/ and the unblock branch n8nfab/hermes-learning-unblock-20261015): step outcome_feedback_agent of config/pipelines/hermes_learning.json stage learn (crontab line 696 as absorbed by the C1 flip; runs today inside run_hermes_pipeline.sh --stage learn --apply). Called only by the process workflow tradeai-fabric-hermes-learning through Run Lane, never by the generic dispatcher (no dispatch block). Was SHADOW ONLY (live_arg null, registry stage shadow) until the 2026-10-17 FEEDBACK CUTOVER at the end of this text; it is LIVE at canary now. lock and lock_kind are the step command's own lock; the dry run takes <lock>.dryrun. timeout_s = the manifest step timeout (5m). --dry-run wins over --apply, sets the DB session read-only, writes no file and never reaches the notifier (scripts/hermes_outcome_feedback_agent.py run). Not a sender in this entry: the dry run sends nothing. The live (cron) sends are declared notification intents through the host chokepoint (send_telegram priority P2/P3, producer hermes_outcome_feedback_agent; AGENTS.md §24.1, §9.1); a live fabric entry must add --notify record (no sender called; intents returned in the RunReceipt for n8n to request through the send-intent route) - cutover prerequisite. The cron step's --apply is the live argument; it is NOT in this entry. offpeak_gate (2026-10-15, cutover prerequisite G4): the cron step runs inside run_with_deepseek_offpeak.sh (default --gate); a LIVE run from n8n reproduces that PEAK_SKIP in the executor (scripts/n8n_run_executor.py offpeak_verdict, the same scripts/lib/deepseek_offpeak.py window), a dry run records the verdict only. Operator route (2026-10-15, cutover prerequisite G5): the live fabric argv is --apply --notify queue (config/n8n_fabric_processes.json cutover_live_arg): each eligible closed-loop alert is QUEUED as a host comms intent (scripts/lib/host_comms_intents.py -> the coordination ledger comms_intents table, route research/hermes_closed_loop_alert in config/host_comms_intent_routes.json), and the host comms-intent consumer turns it into an incident for the incident notifier (P2 digest). The lane calls no sender and n8n never sees or sends the message. | 2026-10-17 FEEDBACK CUTOVER (operator 2026-10-17 "fix now move to n8n now"; n8n cutover directive 2026-10-15: all families to n8n; packet docs/ops/packets/hermes-feedback-cutover-20261017/cutover.sh): live_arg [--apply, --notify, queue] = the spec's cutover_live_arg (G5b; the earlier '--notify record' wording above is superseded by that operator route), registry stage canary, effect key cron_claim true (since PR-1), the same shape as the four learn lanes cut over 2026-10-16. Held until now because the queue argv's 'notify' word tripped the allowlist sender-token gates; those gates now admit exactly ('hermes-learning-outcome-feedback-agent', live_arg [--apply, --notify, queue]) as a queue-only, no-sender argv (scripts/lib/lane_dispatch.py QUEUE_ONLY_NOTIFY_ARGV) and keep refusing --notify chokepoint / record, any other notify value and any other lane. Cron keeps --notify chokepoint (the default) until n8n owns the effect key; after the owner switch the cron stage runner records skipped_effect for this step.
